newsitem.title: USA: CFTC freezes assets of California commodity fund.
newsitem.headline: CFTC freezes assets of California commodity fund.

text.p: The Commodity Futures Trading Commission said Wednesday it obtained a preliminary injunction in federal court freezing the assets of a California commodity investment fund run by Edward Schroeder.
The commission charged that Schroeder used deceptive advertising, failed to register as a commodity pool operator and converted $3 million of his fund's assets to personal use.

The preliminary injunction, stemming from a nine-count civil complaint filed by the CFTC in July, also prohibits Schroeder from further soliciting customers or committing violations of the Commodity Exchange Act.
Also named in the CFTC complaint was Andre Fite and the fund itself, Edward W. Schroeder Living Trust, which was set up in August, 1994.
"Schroeder treated pool funds as his own property, using them to pay his personal expenses and to make deposits into his personal bank accounts," the CFTC complaint alleged.
The complaint alleged that while the fund suffered over $1 million in commodity trading losses, Schroeder assured customers that he was earning high profits.
